info.title: SunCharts API
info.description:
Build your own backend on SunCharts. Everything you need is here: this reference, a free sandbox and
public SDKs. The API is plain HTTPS + JSON, so any language works; the SDKs are optional conveniences.
Machine-readable spec: [`/openapi.json`](/openapi.json) (also `/api/v1/openapi.yaml`).

# Quickstart

1. **Get sandbox credentials** — open the partner console at
   [`https://sandbox-api.suncharts.app/partners/`](https://sandbox-api.suncharts.app/partners/), create a sandbox
   account (email link, no password), then **Create app**. Copy the `client_id` and `client_secret` (shown once).
2. **Get an access token** (OAuth2 client credentials):

```bash
curl -s https://sandbox-api.suncharts.app/oauth/token \
  -u "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -d grant_type=client_credentials -d scope="partner.read tenants.read"
# {"access_token":"pt_…","token_type":"Bearer","expires_in":3600,"scope":"partner.read tenants.read"}
```

3. **Call the API**:

```bash
curl -s https://sandbox-api.suncharts.app/api/v1/partner/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

4. **Or use an SDK** (see *SDKs*; Rust shown — PHP, Python and TypeScript work the same way):

```toml
[dependencies]
suncharts-sdk = { git = "https://github.com/PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-rust", tag = "v0.4.0" }
```

```rust
let client = suncharts_sdk::Client::builder(suncharts_sdk::SANDBOX_BASE_URL)
    .client_credentials(std::env::var("CLIENT_ID")?, std::env::var("CLIENT_SECRET")?)
    .build()?;
let me = client.partner_me().await?; // token fetched, cached and refreshed for you
```

# Environments

| Environment | Base URL | Data |
|---|---|---|
| Sandbox | `https://sandbox-api.suncharts.app` | Simulated EHR data; reset nightly 03:15 America/Chicago (partner accounts, apps and keys are kept) |
| Production | `https://api.suncharts.app` | Real clinics |

Sandbox and production are separate systems: credentials from one never work on the other. Sandbox keys
start with `sk_test_`, production keys with `sk_live_`. Sandbox apps cannot hold `clinical.write`.

**Sandbox test data.** Every sandbox partner gets a tenant `<your-partner-slug>-test` ("Sandbox Test Clinic") with passwordless users `test.owner@example.test` (owner) and `test.clinician@example.test` (clinician); it shows up in `GET /api/v1/partner/tenants` and is re-created after the nightly reset. Sandbox apps start with `email_delivery: partner`, so relayed `auth/magic/*`, signup and invite calls return the `delivery` secret instead of sending mail, and passkey ceremonies use your app's `rp_id`/`auth_origin` exactly as in production.
`sandbox-api.p.industries` and `htpi.p.industries` are legacy aliases; use the hosts above.

# Authentication

Two ways to authenticate your **server** (never ship either to a browser or mobile app):

## OAuth2 client credentials (recommended)

`POST /oauth/token` per [RFC 6749 §4.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-4.4). Send client
authentication as HTTP Basic (`client_id:client_secret`) **or** as `client_id` / `client_secret` body fields;
the body may be `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or JSON. Optional `scope` narrows the token to a subset of
your app's scopes. Tokens (`pt_…`) last **1 hour**; request a new one when `expires_in` runs out (the SDK
does this). Errors follow RFC 6749 §5.2: `invalid_request`, `invalid_client` (401), `unsupported_grant_type`,
`invalid_scope`. `POST /api/v1/partner/token` remains as a legacy JSON alias.

## API keys

Long-lived keys created in the partner console, optionally with an expiry and a subset of the app's scopes.
Send as `Authorization: Bearer sk_…` or `X-API-Key: sk_…`.

**Where to send partner credentials.** Every partner endpoint also accepts them as `X-Partner-Authorization: Bearer <token or key>`; it is checked first, so one request can carry your credentials there and an end user's token in `Authorization`. A `401` caused by partner credentials carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="partner"` — fetch a new access token and retry once. Prefer OAuth2 for production; use keys where a
token exchange is impractical.

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `partner.read` | Your partner profile, branding and app identity; read auth settings |
| `tenants.read` / `tenants.write` | List / create your clinics (tenants) |
| `users.passthrough` | Relay end-user sign-in for your users (see *White-label auth relay*) |
| `clinical.read` / `clinical.write` | Clinical endpoints (with the end user's token) |
| `apps.manage` | Change your app's auth settings via the API |

## Rotation and revocation

Everything is self-serve in the partner console (`/partners/` on each environment):
- **Rotate client secret** — a new secret is issued; the previous one keeps working for a grace window
  (default 24 h, up to 7 days) so you can roll deploys without downtime.
- **Rotate API key** — issues a replacement with the same scopes; the old key expires after the grace window.
- **Revoke** an app or key — takes effect immediately; outstanding access tokens stop working.
- Every issue, rotation, revocation and denied token request is in the console's audit log.

## End-user tokens

Clinical calls run as a clinic user. Your backend signs the user in through the auth endpoints (below) and
uses the returned user access token (`userBearer`). Refresh with `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`.

# White-label auth relay

Your backend can call the end-user auth endpoints (`/api/v1/auth/*`, `/api/v1/signup*`,
`/api/v1/invites/*`, `/api/v1/tenant/invites*`) on behalf of your users so they only ever see your brand.
Identify your app on those calls with:

```
X-Partner-Authorization: Bearer <OAuth access token or API key>   (scope users.passthrough)
X-End-User-IP: 203.0.113.7                                         (optional; per-user rate limits)
```

Without the header, the endpoints behave as for first-party apps. On relayed calls `device_nonce` is optional (secrets are bound to your app) and no CAPTCHA is required. With it, your app's **auth settings** apply:

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| `auth_origin` | Your web origin (e.g. `https://app.example.com`): passkey origin and base for links |
| `rp_id` | Passkey relying-party ID (your domain; must be the origin host or a parent of it) |
| `android_cert_sha256[]` | Your Android signing-cert fingerprints; accepted as passkey origins (`android:apk-key-hash:…`) |
| `apple_app_ids[]` | `TEAMID.bundle.id` of your iOS apps (for your associated-domains file) |
| `email_link_base` | Link target for sign-in emails; `{token}` placeholder, else `#t=<token>` is appended |
| `email_delivery` | `partner` or `platform` (below) |

Set them in the console or with `PATCH /api/v1/partner/auth-settings`. Passkey registration and sign-in then
use your RP ID, origins and brand name.

**Email delivery.** With `partner` delivery we send nothing: `auth/magic/start`, `signup/start`, `signup` and
`signup/resend` return a `delivery` object (`email`, `token`, `code`, `purpose`, `expires_in_mins`) on your
partner-authenticated call only, and you deliver it however you like (`delivery` is `null` when there is
nothing to send, e.g. an unknown email on sign-in). With `platform` delivery we send the email under your brand
and from-address with links on your origin — available once your custom domain is verified; until then those
calls return `409 partner_delivery_required`. Clinic invites for your tenants link to your `auth_origin`.

# Implementing a client (any language)

The contract is the HTTP described here; nothing depends on an SDK. A conforming client:

- **Transport** — HTTPS only, TLS 1.2+. Request and response bodies are UTF-8 JSON
  (`Content-Type: application/json`) except `POST /oauth/token`, which also takes
  `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Send a descriptive `User-Agent` (e.g. `acme-backend/1.4 php/8.3`).
- **Data types** — timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-10-16T16:00:00Z`); dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`;
  IDs are opaque strings (don't parse them, don't assume UUIDs or length). Absent and `null` mean the same.
  **Ignore unknown fields and enum values** you don't recognise: v1 grows additively.
- **Token handling** — cache the `access_token` per (client_id, scope) and reuse it until about 60 s before
  `expires_in` elapses; then request a new one (there are no refresh tokens for client credentials). On a
  `401` from an API call, fetch a fresh token **once** and retry; if it fails again, surface the error.
  Never log `client_secret`, access tokens or API keys.
- **Errors** — branch on HTTP status and the `error` code (see *Errors*), never on `message`. On `409`,
  sub-codes are the text before the first `:` in `message` (e.g. `partner_delivery_required`).
- **Retries** — retry `429` after `Retry-After` seconds, and `502/503/504` and network errors on idempotent
  requests (`GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) with exponential backoff and jitter (e.g. 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s; max 3 tries).
  Don't blindly retry `POST` auth calls (they may send an email).
- **Relay** — on end-user auth calls made for your users, add `X-Partner-Authorization: Bearer <token or key>`
  and `X-End-User-IP`. Pass the end user's own `Authorization` header (if any) through unchanged.
- **Timeouts** — 10 s connect, 30 s total is a good default; FHIR calls proxy to the clinic's EHR and can be
  slower.

### Minimal flow with plain HTTP

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s https://sandbox-api.suncharts.app/oauth/token -u "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -d grant_type=client_credentials | jq -r .access_token)
curl -s https://sandbox-api.suncharts.app/api/v1/partner/tenants -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# relayed sign-in for one of your users, with partner delivery:
curl -s https://sandbox-api.suncharts.app/api/v1/auth/magic/start \
  -H "X-Partner-Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-End-User-IP: 203.0.113.7" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"dr.lee@example.com"}'
# {"status":"sent","message":"…","resend_after":60,"expires_in":600,"code_length":6,
#  "delivery":{"email":"dr.lee@example.com","token":"…","code":"123456","purpose":"signin","expires_in_mins":10}}
```

# Errors

Errors are JSON with a stable, brand-neutral code:

```json
{"error": "bad_request", "message": "human-readable detail"}
```

| HTTP | `error` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `bad_request` | Invalid input |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing, expired or revoked credentials (`invalid_client` on `/oauth/token`) |
| 403 | `forbidden` | Credential lacks the scope / access |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such resource (or not yours) |
| 409 | `conflict` | State conflict (`message` starts with a sub-code such as `partner_delivery_required`) |
| 428 | `openemr_link_required` / `openemr_relink_required` | The user must (re)link their EHR account |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Slow down; honour `Retry-After` |
| 424 | `upstream_error` | The clinic's EHR failed or timed out; retry idempotent calls with backoff |
| 5xx | `internal` | Our side; retry with backoff |

Codes are only ever added within v1.

# Rate limits

- Per app: `rate_limit_per_min` (default **600/min**) shared by its tokens and keys.
- Token endpoint: 30 requests/min per source IP.
- Auth endpoints: per end user (send `X-End-User-IP` when relaying) and per email.
- Exceeding a limit returns `429` with `Retry-After` (seconds). Back off and retry.

# Versioning

- The major version is in the path (`/api/v1`). Within v1 changes are **additive only**: new endpoints,
  new optional request fields, new response fields, new error codes. Ignore unknown fields.
- Breaking changes ship as `/api/v2` with at least **6 months** of overlap. Deprecated operations are marked
  `deprecated` here and answer with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers before removal.
- The SDKs follow SemVer independently of the API version; minor versions add features, patch versions fix bugs.

# SDKs

Official SDKs are generated from this spec ([`/openapi.json`](/openapi.json)) on every API change, plus a thin
hand-written layer for OAuth2 token caching/refresh, API keys, the relay header, retries and pagination.

| Language | Repository | Install | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| PHP 8.2+ | [`PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-php`](https://github.com/PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-php) | `composer require pindustries/suncharts-sdk-php` (VCS repo until published) | MIT |
| Rust | [`PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-rust`](https://github.com/PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-rust) | `suncharts-sdk = { git = "https://github.com/PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-rust", tag = "v0.4.0" }` | MIT OR Apache-2.0 |
| Python 3.9+ | [`PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-python`](https://github.com/PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-python) | `pip install "git+https://github.com/PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-python@v0.1.0"` | MIT |
| TypeScript / Node 18+ | [`PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-typescript`](https://github.com/PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-typescript) | `npm install github:PIndustries/suncharts-sdk-typescript#v0.1.0` | MIT |

Any other language — generate a client from [`/openapi.json`](/openapi.json).

post.description: RFC 6749 §4.4. Client auth via HTTP Basic or body fields. Response has `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.summary: Partner, branding and app identity (scope partner.read)

post.summary: End-user sign-in (passthrough from the partner backend)

200.description: Session, or a clinic selection when the email belongs to several clinics

post.description: Legacy password sign-in (may be disabled on a deployment). Prefer passkeys or email magic links.

get.summary: EHR (OpenEMR) connections visible to the user

200.description: Session, or a clinic selection when the email belongs to several clinics

post.summary: Email a single-use sign-in link + 6-digit code
post.description: Enumeration-safe: identical response whether or not the email has an account. 60 s resend cooldown.

409.description: partner_delivery_required (relay, platform delivery without a verified custom domain)

post.summary: Redeem a magic link or code (same device only)

200.description: Session, or a clinic selection when the email belongs to several clinics

patch.summary: Update your app's auth settings (omitted = unchanged, ""/[] = clear)

post.summary: Passwordless sign-up: email + clinic name → link/code
post.description: Body: `email`, `clinic_name`, `accept_terms`, `terms_version`, `device_nonce`, optional `display_name`. Relay + partner delivery returns `delivery`.
Returns `ceremony_id` and `options` (publicKey request). Relay: partner RP ID/origins.

get.summary: Users of one of your tenants

post.summary: Invite a user to one of your tenants
post.description: Replaces any outstanding invite for the same email. `409` if the email already has an account in the tenant. Delivery follows your app's `email_delivery` (see *White-label auth relay*).
Signs the user out everywhere and drops their EHR links. Idempotent. `409` if it would leave the tenant without an active owner.

partnerBearer.description: pt_… access token from POST /oauth/token, or an sk_… API key

scopes.partner.read: Partner profile, branding, app identity, auth settings (read)
scopes.users.passthrough: Relay end-user auth for your users

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: Partner API key (sk_live_… / sk_test_…). Also accepted as Authorization: Bearer sk_…

partnerHeader.name: X-Partner-Authorization
partnerHeader.description: `Bearer <pt_… access token | sk_… API key>`. Accepted on every partner endpoint and preferred when your request also carries an end user's `Authorization`. Checked before `Authorization` and `X-API-Key`.

PartnerAuthorization.name: X-Partner-Authorization
PartnerAuthorization.description: White-label relay: `Bearer <pt_… token | sk_… key>` of the partner app (scope users.passthrough). Applies the app's auth settings.

EndUserIp.name: X-End-User-IP
EndUserIp.description: Relay only: the end user's IP for rate limiting.

error.description: Stable machine code. Known values: `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `bad_request`, `conflict`, `rate_limited`, `mfa_required`, `mfa_invalid`, `mfa_enrollment_required`, `openemr_link_required`, `openemr_relink_required`, `upstream_error`, `internal`. New codes may be added within v1: treat unknown values like the HTTP status.

message.description: Human-readable detail (do not branch on it; on 409 the text before the first `:` is a sub-code)

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait (on `rate_limited`; also sent as `Retry-After`)

data.description: Same as `tenants` (kept for early v1 clients).

next_cursor.description: Reserved for pagination; currently always null (every tenant is returned in one page).

tenant.description: DEPRECATED. Clinic code is no longer needed: the email is looked up across clinics. If sent, it only narrows the clinics the credentials already prove; any mismatch returns the same generic 401.

tenant_id.description: Optional: choose this clinic when the account belongs to several.

LoginRequest.description: Legacy password sign-in (server flag SUNCHARTS_USER_PASSWORD_LOGIN). Prefer passkeys or email magic links.

ClinicSelection.description: Returned instead of tokens when the email belongs to several clinics. Call /api/v1/auth/login/select with one tenant_id.

device_nonce.description: 16-200 random chars, stable per device; links/codes are bound to it. Required for first-party calls; optional on partner-relayed calls (with X-Partner-Authorization), where they are bound to your app instead.

MagicVerifyRequest.description: Either token (from the link) or email + 6-digit code.

device_nonce.description: 16-200 random chars, stable per device; links/codes are bound to it. Required for first-party calls; optional on partner-relayed calls (with X-Partner-Authorization), where they are bound to your app instead.

Delivery.description: Partner email delivery only: the secret to deliver to the user (never present without X-Partner-Authorization).

scope.description: Space-separated subset of the app's scopes

role.description: owner | clinician | front_desk | read_only (new roles may be added)

InviteDelivery.description: `transport: partner` → we sent nothing; deliver `url` (or build your own from `token`). Otherwise the mail transport's result.

code.description: Always null for invites (there is no code to enter)
